questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes You must answer on the multiple choice answer sheet. You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS  There are forty questions on this paper. Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 40.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.

This introduced a source of error into the experiment. Which statements about this error are correct?

questions.questionText: The graph shows the results of two experiments on the effect of increasing substrate concentration on the rate of an enzyme-catalysed reaction. One experiment was at a high concentration of enzyme and the second was at a low concentration of enzyme. All other variables were standardised. high enzyme concentration low enzyme initial rate X concentration of reaction substrate concentration What would limit the initial rate of reaction at point X?

options.C: substrate concentration

questions.questionText: Which statements about the Michaelis–Menten constant (K ) of an enzyme are correct? m
Which component of cell surface membranes helps to reduce fluidity of the phospholipids at high temperatures?

options.C: cholesterol

questions.questionText: Plant cells were left for 50 minutes in three different sugar solutions, 10%, 5% and 1%. The water potential in the cytoplasm of the three cells was the same at the start of the experiment. The diagrams show the appearance of the cells after 50 minutes, using a light microscope. cell P cell Q cell R Which conclusion is correct?

options.A: Cell P has the same concentration of sugar inside and outside the cell.
options.B: Cell Q is flaccid and cell P is plasmolysed.
options.C: Cell Q was placed in the 1% solution.
options.D: The sugar solution outside cell R has a less negative water potential than inside cell R.

options.C: volume surface area decreases

questions.questionText: A human embryo consists of 12 cells at the start of day 1. The cells divide by mitosis for 4 complete days at a rate of 1 division every 32 hours. What is the maximum number of cells in the embryo at the end of day 4?

options.C: 192 cells

options.C: It occurs from source to sink.

questions.questionText: Which statement correctly describes infectious diseases?

options.A: They are diseases caused by environmental factors that are not passed from one person to another.
options.B: They are diseases caused by a fault in the DNA that can be passed from a parent to their offspring.
options.C: They are diseases caused by a lack of a nutrient in the diet, such as a vitamin or mineral.
options.D: They are diseases caused by a pathogen such as a bacterium, fungus, protoctist or virus.

questions.questionText: A patient has had repeated infections from the same pathogen over a few months. The patient has been treated with the same antibiotic on each occasion. Which treatment could prevent an increase in the antibiotic resistance of the pathogen?

options.A: a narrow spectrum antibiotic to treat a non-cellular pathogen
options.B: a repeat prescription for the same antibiotic at a higher dose
options.C: a specific antibiotic after testing for the pathogen
options.D: a wide spectrum antibiotic to treat different strains of the pathogen

questions.questionText: A patient with kidney failure can be given a kidney transplant. In a kidney transplant, a healthy kidney is taken from another person and put into the patient’s body. Sometimes the donated kidney cells are killed by the patient’s body. In this primary immune response, T-lymphocytes bind to antigens on the donated kidney cells and are activated. The statements describe the next stages of the primary immune response.

options.A: U and X allow the antibody to bind to two different antigens.
options.B: V allows the antibody to be flexible to bind to two antigens.
options.C: W can bind to one specific antigen.
